game.title: Sudoku
game.selectCellHint: Select a cell to enter a number
game.gameOverMessage: You reached the mistake limit ({{limit}}). Better luck next time!

controls.keyboard: Use keys 1-9, arrows for navigation, Backspace to clear, N for notes, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y for undo/redo

hint.title: Hint
hint.noHint: No hint available for this position.

NAKED_SINGLE.name: Naked Single
NAKED_SINGLE.explanation: Cell R{{row}}C{{col}} has only one possible candidate — {{value}}. All other digits are already present in its row, column, or box.

HIDDEN_SINGLE.name: Hidden Single
HIDDEN_SINGLE.explanation: Digit {{value}} can only go in cell R{{row}}C{{col}} within its house. Every other cell in that row, column, or box already rules out {{value}}.

LOCKED_CANDIDATES.name: Locked Candidates
LOCKED_CANDIDATES.explanation: A digit is confined to a single row or column within a box (or vice versa). This lets us eliminate that digit from the rest of the row, column, or box.

NAKED_PAIR.name: Naked Pair
NAKED_PAIR.explanation: Two cells in the same house share exactly the same two candidates. Those digits can be eliminated from all other cells in that house.

HIDDEN_PAIR.name: Hidden Pair
HIDDEN_PAIR.explanation: Two digits appear as candidates in exactly two cells of a house. All other candidates can be removed from those two cells.

NAKED_TRIPLE.name: Naked Triple
NAKED_TRIPLE.explanation: Three cells in a house collectively contain exactly three candidate digits. Those digits can be eliminated from the rest of the house.

HIDDEN_TRIPLE.name: Hidden Triple
HIDDEN_TRIPLE.explanation: Three digits appear in exactly three cells of a house. All other candidates can be removed from those cells.

NAKED_QUAD.name: Naked Quad
NAKED_QUAD.explanation: Four cells in a house collectively contain exactly four candidate digits. Those digits can be eliminated from the rest of the house.

HIDDEN_QUAD.name: Hidden Quad
HIDDEN_QUAD.explanation: Four digits appear in exactly four cells of a house. All other candidates can be removed from those cells.

X_WING.name: X-Wing
X_WING.explanation: A digit appears in exactly two cells in each of two rows, and those cells share the same two columns. The digit can be eliminated from those columns in all other rows.

SWORDFISH.name: Swordfish
SWORDFISH.explanation: A digit appears in exactly two or three cells across three rows, all confined to the same three columns. It can be eliminated from those columns in all other rows.

JELLYFISH.name: Jellyfish
JELLYFISH.explanation: A digit appears in two to four cells across four rows, confined to the same four columns. It can be eliminated from those columns in all other rows.

XY_WING.name: XY-Wing
XY_WING.explanation: A pivot cell with two candidates {X,Y} is connected to two pincers: one with {X,Z} and one with {Y,Z}. Any cell that sees both pincers cannot contain Z.

XYZ_WING.name: XYZ-Wing
XYZ_WING.explanation: A pivot with three candidates {X,Y,Z} is connected to two bivalue pincers that together cover all three. Z can be eliminated from cells that see all three.

W_WING.name: W-Wing
W_WING.explanation: Two bivalue cells share the same candidate pair {A,B} and are connected by a strong link on A. Digit B can be eliminated from cells that see both.

UNIQUE_RECTANGLE_1.name: Unique Rectangle Type 1
UNIQUE_RECTANGLE_1.explanation: Three corners of a rectangle contain only the same two candidates. Placing those digits in the fourth corner would create two solutions, so they must be eliminated from it.

UNIQUE_RECTANGLE_2.name: Unique Rectangle Type 2
UNIQUE_RECTANGLE_2.explanation: Two diagonal corners of a rectangle each have one extra candidate X beyond the shared pair. Since at least one must place X, it can be eliminated from cells that see both.

SIMPLE_COLORING.name: Simple Coloring
SIMPLE_COLORING.explanation: Strong links on a digit form a chain. Cells at alternating chain positions are colored. Either a color group is self-contradicting (wrap) or cells seeing both colors cannot contain the digit (trap).

ANTI_KNIGHT.name: Anti-Knight
ANTI_KNIGHT.description: Classic rules + same digits cannot be a knight's move apart

ODD_EVEN.name: Odd-Even
ODD_EVEN.description: Classic rules + marked cells must contain odd or even digits

ANTI_KING.name: Anti-King
ANTI_KING.description: Classic rules + same digits cannot be adjacent (king's move)

NON_CONSECUTIVE.name: Non-Consecutive
NON_CONSECUTIVE.description: Classic rules + adjacent cells cannot differ by 1

KROPKI.name: Kropki
KROPKI.description: Classic rules + white dot=diff 1, black dot=×2 between neighbours

KILLER.name: Killer
KILLER.description: Classic rules + cages with target sums, no digit repeats in cage

LITTLE_KILLER.name: Little Killer
LITTLE_KILLER.description: Classic rules + diagonal sums shown outside the grid (digits may repeat)

GREATER_THAN.name: Greater Than
GREATER_THAN.description: Classic rules + inequality signs between adjacent cells must be satisfied

THERMO.name: Thermo
THERMO.description: Classic rules + digits must strictly increase along each thermometer from bulb to tip

SANDWICH.name: Sandwich
SANDWICH.description: Classic rules + clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between 1 and 9
